segments.text: So, what did you try next?
Well, I started putting my meals onto a smaller plate, to reduce the portion sizes, you know?
And then I started to take brisk walk round my village after dinner every evening.
It was difficult at first, but when I realised it got me out of the washing up every night,
I started to enjoy escaping for half an hour every evening.
Some friends decided to join me, and before I knew it, I was seeing more of my friends, losing some weight, and becoming less breathless.
Then my husband bought me a gym subscription for my birthday, and that was it. There was no stopping me.
They say that exercise is addictive. Did you find that was true for you?
Definitely. It gave me a new lease of life. I realised I was hooked when I was so full
of energy that I just didn't want to sit down. I clearly remember going for my six-month
check-up at the surgery and when they said I was no longer obese, I almost hugged the
doctor. It was amazing. I felt so much better about myself and was so relieved to feel
healthy again. I think I drove my family a bit mad at the beginning. I was so enthusiastic
and wanted everyone I met to join me in feeling that good. But I know that some people have
serious health problems which prevent them from taking exercise, so that's why I decided
to run the marathons.
Yes, tell us some more about that Gina. How did that come about?
Well, I was watching the London Marathon on the TV, and my youngest son said,
Mum, you can do that. I'd started running, rather than walking around the village by then,
so it seemed like a good thing to aim for, and a good way of raising money for people
with serious heart problems. I ran my first marathon in 2007, and I've done five so far.
7 in 7 days is a bit daunting, but I've been training hard and all my family is supporting
me. I've already raised over £3,000, so I can't let anyone down and back out now.
Well, you're certainly an inspiration to us all. Gina, we wish you every success for
your amazing challenge. We'll be cheering you on. Will you come back to the studio
tell us how you got on. Of course Peter, as soon as I've caught my breath
